source.title: Belfast News-Letter, 17 January 1923, p. 5 ("The municipal elections: the results"); Belfast News-Letter, 6 January 1923, p. 5 ("Ulster local elections: nominations in Belfast")
source.publisher: Belfast News-Letter (via the Irish Newspaper Archives)
source.check: figures read from the page images of the News-Letter's ward results (INA block images) and checked against the Irish News; names and full forms from the News-Letter's list of nominations; unopposed members are the only remaining nominees for the seats after the withdrawals reported on 8 January

note: Election of the whole of Belfast Corporation (an alderman and three councillors in each of the 15 wards) by direct vote, proportional representation having been abolished; nominations 5 January, poll Monday 15 January 1923, counted 16 January. Eight aldermen and nine councillors (St Anne's, Pottinger and Windsor) were returned unopposed at nomination, and withdrawals left the Duncairn and Victoria councillors unopposed (Belfast News-Letter, 6 and 8 January 1923). State of parties in the new Corporation: Official Unionists 43, Independent Unionists 7, Nationalists 3, Labour 2 (News-Letter, 17 January 1923). Crichton stood as the nominee of Unionist ex-servicemen against Mercier, the retiring alderman. The News-Letter prints a majority of 722 and a total poll of 7,459, which do not agree with the two printed votes (difference 631, sum 7,499); Mercier's figure may be a misprint for 3,343.
correctionNote: Corrected from the Belfast Corporation register of members (PRONI LA/7/1/CA/1/3): Samuel Turpin Mercier's vote is 3,343 as the register records it (previously 3,434, from the newspaper source).
